API

Public API ​

Hikari.attach_bump Method
julia
attach_bump(mat, entity, textures) -> mat

Attach entity's height field to mat's displacement. pbrt-v4 master spells it displacement; older .pbrt files use bumpmap. Both are float height fields, read by finite differences at intersection time.

Public because RayMakie's pbrt bridge builds materials before any Hikari scene exists and needs the same attachment — it called this through the underscore when it was private, which is how a rename here became a rename there.

source
Hikari.native_radiative_volume Function
julia
native_radiative_volume(path; mass_unit, black_hole_mass, fade=(11f0, 14f0),
                        normalization=nothing, emission_params=EmissionParams())

The fields of radiative_volume on the snapshot's own spherical grid instead of a Cartesian resampling: emissivity, absorption and the fluid's static-frame Cartesian velocity per native cell, (φ, θ, r), radial shells up to the first one at fade[2], faded out from fade[1] on. The grid comes along as the colatitude of every cell (theta[r, θ]), the log-uniform radial spacing and the uniform azimuth spacing. Radii are in Schwarzschild radii.

source
Hikari.radiative_volume Function
julia
radiative_volume(path; mass_unit, black_hole_mass, resolution=192,
                 extent=15f0, normalization=nothing, emission_params=EmissionParams())

Prepare emissivity, absorption and fluid-velocity fields for a volume medium. Loading a GRMHD snapshot requires loading the optional GRMHDSnapshots package. Coordinates use Schwarzschild radii. No images or display transforms are made. The simulation mass unit and black-hole mass must be supplied in CGS grams; the adapter does not choose a particular astronomical object or flux calibration.

source
Hikari.TextureNodes Module

Builders for node textures, after Blender's shader nodes, with Blender's names, settings and defaults. using Hikari.TextureNodes, then e.g.

julia
p = xyz()
rings = wave(p; type = :rings, scale = 2, distortion = 4, detail = 3).fac
wood = color_ramp(rings, 0.0 => (0.6, 0.35, 0.15), 0.8 => (0.45, 0.25, 0.1), 1.0 => (0.2, 0.1, 0.04))
Hikari.Diffuse(color = wood)

Inputs are uv, xyz (world-space position) and normal. Every socket of a node takes a number, a colour or tuple, or another node's output. Nodes with several outputs return their first and name the others: noise(p).color, voronoi(p).position, brick(p).fac.

Arithmetic (+ - * / ^, min, max, mod (floored), rem, abs, sign, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sqrt, exp, log, the trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, atan(y, x), clamp) works elementwise on nodes and plain numbers or colours, like Blender's Math and Vector Math nodes; dot, cross, norm and normalize come from LinearAlgebra. math and vector_math reach the operations without a Julia function.

source
Hikari.TextureNodes.attribute Method
julia
attribute(name)

Blender's Attribute node in a shader: the mesh's vertex attribute name interpolated over the hit's triangle, as .color (also the vector, the first output) and .fac (its average). The mesh pushed with the shader's material supplies it: a vertex attribute of the GeometryBasics mesh such as :color, with colours read as sRGB and turned linear like Blender's byte colours, numbers and vectors as they are. :generated, :object and :object_normal are the coordinates texture_coordinate names. A mesh without the attribute reads 0.

source

brick(p = xyz(); color1, color2, mortar, scale = 5, mortar_size = 0.02, mortar_smooth = 0.1, bias = 0,
      brick_width = 0.5, row_height = 0.25, offset = 0.5, offset_frequency = 2, squash = 1, squash_frequency = 2)

Blender's Brick Texture; its outputs are color and .fac (1 in the mortar).

Hikari.TextureNodes.bump Method
julia
bump(height; strength = 1, distance = 0.001, filter_width = 0.1, invert = false, normal = normal())

Blender's Bump node: the normal of the surface displaced by distance times height along it, for a shader's normal input. As in Cycles, the height graph is evaluated at the hit and at the hit moved by filter_width of a pixel in either screen direction.

source
Hikari.TextureNodes.color_ramp Method
julia
color_ramp(t, stops...; interpolation = :linear)

Blender's Color Ramp: stops are position => colour pairs (or numbers) in increasing position; t below the first or above the last stop holds the end colour. interpolation is :constant, :linear, :ease, :cardinal or :b_spline. Like Cycles, the ramp is baked into a table of 256 colours.

Blender's Math node, per component for vectors: op is one of its operations by name, e.g. :smooth_min, :wrap, :snap, :pingpong, :compare.

Hikari.TextureNodes.mix Method
julia
mix(a, b, factor; blend = :mix, clamp_factor = false, clamp_result = false)

Blender's Mix node: a towards b by factor, which may be a vector for the plain :mix. blend is one of its colour blend modes, e.g. :multiply, :screen, :overlay, :soft_light, :hue.

source
Hikari.TextureNodes.noise Function
julia
noise(p = xyz(); scale = 5, detail = 2, roughness = 0.5, lacunarity = 2, distortion = 0,
      type = :fbm, normalize = true, offset = 0, gain = 1, w = 0, dimensions = 3)

Blender's Noise Texture. Its outputs are fac and .color. type is :fbm, :multifractal, :hybrid_multifractal, :ridged_multifractal or :hetero_terrain; w is the fourth coordinate for dimensions = 4 and the only one for dimensions = 1.

source
Hikari.TextureNodes.normal Method

Shading normal (world space).

source
Hikari.TextureNodes.normal_map Method
julia
normal_map(color; strength = 1, space = :tangent, invert_green = false)

Blender's Normal Map node: the normal a normal map's color encodes, for a shader's normal input. In :tangent space the colour is read in the frame of the uv map's tangent, bitangent and the shading normal (OpenGL convention: green along increasing v; invert_green reads DirectX maps); :world and :blender_world take it as a world space normal. Object space is not supported.

Hikari.TextureNodes.texture_coordinate Method
julia
texture_coordinate()

Blender's Texture Coordinate node in a shader, its outputs by name: generated (the position in the mesh's bounding box, 0 to 1), normal (the object space normal), uv, object (the object space position), camera (camera space, z along the view), window (the position on the image, 0 to 1 from the bottom left) and reflection (the mirrored view direction, world space).

Apply an affine map to a point: M is a 4×4 matrix (only its top three rows are used) or a 3×3 one. Use the inverse of an object's model matrix to get coordinates that stay attached to the object.

Hikari.TextureNodes.voronoi Function
julia
voronoi(p = xyz(); scale = 5, detail = 0, roughness = 0.5, lacunarity = 2, smoothness = 1, exponent = 0.5,
        randomness = 1, feature = :f1, metric = :euclidean, normalize = false, w = 0, dimensions = 3)

Blender's Voronoi Texture. Its outputs are distance, .color, .position, .w and .radius (for feature = :n_sphere_radius). feature is :f1, :f2, :smooth_f1, :distance_to_edge or :n_sphere_radius; metric is :euclidean, :manhattan, :chebychev or :minkowski (with exponent).

Blender's Wave Texture; its outputs are color and .fac. Bands run along :x, :y, :z or :diagonal, rings around :x, :y, :z or :spherical.

Internal API ​

Hikari.BRICAUD_1995 Constant

Chlorophyll-specific phytoplankton absorption A(λ) (m²/mg, at 1 mg/m³), 400–700 nm: Bricaud et al. 1995, JGR 100, 13321 (via omlc.org).

source
Hikari.CosineLobe Type

The lobes evaluated from cosines alone (cosine_f), isotropic and of no tangent.

source
Hikari.D65_ILLUMINANT_VALUES Constant
julia
D65_ILLUMINANT_VALUES

D65 illuminant spectral power distribution values (normalized to 100 at 560nm).

source
Hikari.D65_ILLUMINANT_WAVELENGTHS Constant
julia
D65_ILLUMINANT_WAVELENGTHS

Wavelength sample points for D65 illuminant spectrum (300-830nm, 5nm intervals).

source
Hikari.DeviceSet Type

A set as device code reads it: the whole StaticMultiTypeSet, or a view of some of its slots (shade_set).

source
Hikari.FEM_DEFAULT_RAMP Constant

The default field ramp: blue at 0, yellow at 1.

A VECTOR of colours and not a name. colormap = :viridis stood here and could not work – FEMFieldTexture takes "any Makie-style colour ramp", which is a vector, and Hikari depends on Colors but on no colormap package, so nothing could turn the symbol into colours. The documented FEMMaterial(cx, cy, cf) therefore failed on its own default; every working caller passed a ramp.

source
Hikari.FEM_RAMP_N Constant

Number of entries in a field texture's colour ramp.

Inline in the struct rather than a second stored array, because a material parameter is ONE TexHandle and a handle carries one (slot, idx). The coefficients get that slot — they scale with the number of cells and a real grid has thousands — so the ramp, which does not, rides along inline.

source
Hikari.FIREFLY_RATIO Constant
julia
weight_color(lum_p, lum_q, sigma) -> Float32

Color/luminance edge-stopping weight in log-luminance space (HDR-safe). sigma is in stops (log2 luminance ratio) — a 2^sigma ratio between p and q weights to exp(-1) ≈ 0.37.

Asymmetric: when q is dimmer than the center p we treat the diff as FIREFLY_RATIO ≈ 0.3× of its actual magnitude, so bright outliers pool down into their dim surroundings (firefly suppression). When q is brighter we stay strict so genuine edges viewed from the dim side are preserved. This is the standard fix for à-trous's intrinsic inability to remove fireflies via a purely symmetric bilateral weight — a firefly otherwise looks like an edge.

There is deliberately no variance term: real SVGF needs temporal variance from sample history, which this Film does not store, and the spatial substitute was actively harmful — it mistakes texture for noise.

source
Hikari.MISS_DEPTH Constant

The depth written where a primary ray hit nothing.

Finite, not Inf, when the scene has an infinite light: the denoiser filters across depth, and a difference against Inf is NaN — with a sky there, the missed pixel is content to be filtered, not missing data. Without one, Inf is kept because it is the honest answer and nothing downstream reads it.

Both are far beyond any scene, so missed reads either, and every consumer asks that instead of testing for one of the two. Testing isinf directly is what made a transparent background come out opaque: with an AmbientLight in the scene the misses were 1f30, no pixel counted as escaped, and the alpha the compositing caller reads was 1 everywhere.

source
Hikari.NAMED_IOR_SPECTRA Constant

pbrt-v4's named spectra of an index of refraction (GetNamedSpectrum): a glass's eta, a metal's eta and k.

source
Hikari.NODE_STACK Constant

The most stack floats a program may use. Each program runs with the smallest of NODE_STACK_SIZES that holds what it uses, stored in bits STACK_SHIFT and up of F: the stack takes thread memory, so a larger one than needed slows the heavier nodes down.

source
Hikari.NT_LEAF_WORDS Constant

Words per node and offsets in words of the fields this file writes and reads (the byte constants of nanovdb.jl over 4).

source
Hikari.POPE_FRY_1997 Constant

Pure water absorption (1/m) by integrating cavity, 380–727.5 nm: Pope & Fry 1997, Appl. Opt. 36, 8710 (via omlc.org).

source
Hikari.PRIMES Constant

First 1023 prime numbers (omitting 2). Used in radical_inverse function.

source
Hikari.SEGELSTEIN_1981 Constant

Pure water absorption (1/m), 300–900 nm, compiled by Segelstein 1981 (via omlc.org): outside Pope & Fry's range.

source
Hikari.SHADING_NORMAL_ARG Constant

The argument code of a BSDF input that is the shading normal; codes from WIDE_CONSTANT_ARG up are folded colours.

source
Hikari.WINDOWED Constant
julia
WINDOWED

The prev_intr_n of a path that left a non-specular vertex in Snell's window and crossed the surface (see snells_window). Light sampling at that vertex reaches the sky it goes to as well, and the crossing put that sampling's density for the path's direction into its r_l, so the escape handler weighs the sky by MIS with the r_l as it is. The next vertex sets its own prev_intr_n, so the mark lasts exactly until the path meets anything. A real one is never zero.

source
Hikari.WYVILL_VOLUME Constant

The integral of Wyvill's kernel (1 - d²/R²)³ over space, over R³: 4π · 16/315.

source
Hikari._PRINCIPLED_UNREAD Constant

The Principled BSDF inputs, by position, that each weight leaves unread when it is zero.

source
Hikari.AbstractLobeStorage Type

A bounded lobe collection implementing mixture, sample selection and subsurface access.

source
Hikari.Add Type
julia
Add(a, b)

Blender's Add Shader: the lobes of both, which is not energy conserving in general. Both must be BSDFs a shader graph holds (Principled, Diffuse, Glass, Refraction, Glossy, Metallic, Translucent, Sheen, Toon, SubsurfaceScattering, Transparent, Emission, and mixes and sums of them).

source
Hikari.AeratedMedium Type
julia
AeratedMedium(foam, bubbles; bounds, radius, σ_a, σ_s, onset, full, foamσ, air, g = 0.8, airg = 0.8,
              merge = radius / 3, lattice = 3, ior = 1.33, weight = Returns(1), backend)

The medium inside a MetaballSurface of water, with the whitewater's air in it as particles, the way the water's surface is its particles: the water absorbs σ_a and scatters σ_s (per metre, RGB) everywhere in bounds, and the air scatters white on top. Each particle stands for its share of air over radius (Wyvill's kernel, as the surface's, normalised to particles per cubic metre). The bubbles are a haze: air square metres of cross-section each. The foam, which floats in a thin layer on the water, is all bubbles or none: where its density rises from onset to full particles per cubic metre it turns to foam scattering foamσ per metre, the iso level of its particles as the water's surface is of its own. g is the Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry of the water's sediment. A particle at p stands for weight(p) of one: a weight falling to zero towards the edge of the water drawn fades the air out there instead of cutting it off.

The air scatters forward too, as airg says, and dense foam scatters hundreds of times before light gets out of it; it is drawn by the similarity relation instead (Zhao, Ramamoorthi & Bala 2014): scattering σ_s (1 - airg) with no preferred direction, which diffuses light the same in a fifth of the scattering events. The trackers take the water as the control of decomposition tracking (see control) and look up only the air.

The air's densities are the particles' kernel sums, cached: particles closer than merge are merged into one at their centre, the cells radius wide over bounds that any particle reaches get a brick of the sums at lattice + 1 points a side, evaluated on backend, and a lookup interpolates its brick trilinearly. A sum over the particles took hundreds of terms where the foam crowds, at every step a ray took through it; the brick is one fetch, and its largest sample bounds the cell exactly, which makes the cell's majorant.

The water lies under a surface of index ior: light sampling inside it samples the sky through Snell's window (see snells_window).

source
Hikari.AirParticles Type
julia
AirParticles

The merged air particles sorted into the medium's cells, as the kernel that fills the bricks reads them.

source
Hikari.AliasTable Type
julia
AliasTable{V1,V2}

Walker's alias method for O(1) sampling from a discrete distribution. Each bin stores:

  • p: The PMF (probability) for this index

  • q: The threshold for choosing this index vs the alias

  • alias: The aliased index if u > q

Following pbrt-v4's implementation in util/sampling.h

Parameterized to work with both CPU (Vector) and GPU arrays (CLArray, etc.)

source
Hikari.AliasTable Method
julia
AliasTable(weights::AbstractVector{Float32})

Construct an alias table from weights (need not sum to 1).

source
Hikari.AmbientLight Method
julia
AmbientLight(rgb::RGB{Float32})

Create an AmbientLight from RGB color with automatic spectral conversion and photometric normalization, matching pbrt-v4's UniformInfiniteLight creation: scale = 1 / SpectrumToPhotometric(spectrum).

Example

julia
light = AmbientLight(RGB{Float32}(0.1f0, 0.1f0, 0.1f0))
source
Hikari.Anisotropic Type
julia
Anisotropic(; ratio = 4, neighbours = 25)

Kernels shaped by the particles round them (Yu & Turk 2013, "Reconstructing surfaces of particle-based fluids using anisotropic kernels"): each particle's kernel is an ellipsoid along the principal axes of its neighbours' weighted spread, its longest axis the metaballs' radius (so it reaches no further than a ball, and the cells still hold all that touches them) and the others shorter by the ratio of the spread's standard deviations along them, down to 1/ratio of it. (Yu & Turk's ratio of the variances, unsmoothed positions given, thinned kernels until the surface tore into dark holes at a whirlpool's lip.) A particle in a flat layer of water gets a flat kernel and the surface over the layer is flat, where balls left it lumpy at their own spacing; thin sheets and filaments stay thin. A particle with fewer than neighbours within the radius keeps a ball. Each kernel is scaled by the ratio of a ball's volume to its own, as Yu & Turk's det G, so that it adds as much to the field as a ball would.

Hikari.BVHLightSampler Type
julia
BVHLightSampler

Spatially-aware light sampler using a BVH over bounded lights. Default light sampler in pbrt-v4 (lightsamplers.h:259-404).

Construction builds the BVH on CPU from light bounds. The resulting node array and bit trail array are uploaded to GPU for kernel use.

Build a BVHLightSampler from a MultiTypeSet of lights. Separates infinite and bounded lights, builds BVH over bounded lights.

Simple box filter with constant weight 1.0 within the support region. This is the simplest filter - uniform sampling within the pixel.

Hikari.CIEXYZTable Method
julia
CIEXYZTable() -> CIEXYZTable{Vector{Float32},Vector{Float32},Vector{Float32}}

Create the default CPU CIE XYZ table from built-in data.

source
Hikari.ClosureQueue Type
julia
ClosureQueue{M}(queues, slot, inputs)

The hits of slot slot of queues, shaded by BSDF kernel class M, with any computed inputs their values kernel gathered. M is a node tuple or a bounded runtime storage class. It excludes the shader's value program and, for runtime storage, its exact node combination and ordering.

source
Hikari.CoatedConductor Type
julia
CoatedConductor(; interface_roughness = 0, interface_ior = 1.5, conductor_ior, conductor_extinction,
                reflectance, conductor_roughness = 0.01, thickness = 0.01, albedo = (0, 0, 0), g = 0,
                max_depth = 10, n_samples = 1, remap_roughness = true, displacement = nothing)

pbrt-v4's coated conductor: a dielectric coat over a Conductor, with a slab of medium between them, its BSDF estimated by a random walk between the two (pbrt's LayeredBxDF).

  • interface_roughness, interface_ior: the coat's roughness (one value or (u, v)) and IOR, a number or a spectrum that disperses the path's wavelengths.

  • conductor_ior, conductor_extinction: the metal's complex IOR, colours or spectra; or instead its reflectance, its colour at normal incidence. Neither is pbrt's default, copper.

  • conductor_roughness: the metal's, one value or (u, v).

  • thickness, albedo, g, max_depth, n_samples, remap_roughness: as CoatedDiffuse's.

The conductor's IOR is taken relative to the coat's, as pbrt-v4 does.

source
Hikari.CoatedDiffuse Type
julia
CoatedDiffuse(; reflectance = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), roughness = 0, thickness = 0.01, ior = 1.5,
              albedo = (0, 0, 0), g = 0, max_depth = 10, n_samples = 1, remap_roughness = true,
              displacement = nothing)

pbrt-v4's coated diffuse: a dielectric coat over a diffuse base, with a slab of medium between them, its BSDF estimated by a random walk between the two (pbrt's LayeredBxDF).

  • reflectance: the base's albedo; its alpha cuts the surface out.

  • roughness: the coat's, one value or (u, v); with remap_roughness the GGX alpha is pbrt's of it.

  • thickness, albedo, g: the slab's thickness, and its medium's single-scattering albedo (0 is none) and Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry.

  • ior: the coat's, a number or a spectrum that disperses the path's wavelengths.

  • max_depth, n_samples: the random walk's length and how many it averages.

source
Hikari.CoatedDiffuseTransmission Type
julia
CoatedDiffuseTransmission(; reflectance = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), transmittance = (0.25, 0.25, 0.25), roughness = 0,
                          thickness = 0.01, ior = 1.5, albedo = (0, 0, 0), g = 0, max_depth = 10,
                          n_samples = 1, remap_roughness = true, displacement = nothing)

A dielectric coat over a DiffuseTransmission base, as CoatedDiffuse coats a diffuse one (pbrt-v4's LayeredBxDF<DielectricBxDF, DiffuseTransmissionBxDF, true>): leaves, thin fabric, paper with a glossy surface.

source
Hikari.CompiledProgram Type

A compiled node program before it is linked: its instructions, each read of a stored array (an image, a mesh attribute) holding the read's ordinal where the array's place goes, and the data of the reads in that order. Compiling stores nothing: link puts in where each datum is stored, and where that is is decided by place!, so a program pushed new and a program replacing another compile the same way and differ only in where their data goes.

source
Hikari.Conductor Type
julia
Conductor(; ior = (0.2, 0.2, 0.2), extinction = (3.9, 3.9, 3.9), roughness = 0.1, remap_roughness = true,
          displacement = nothing)
Conductor(; reflectance, roughness = 0.1, remap_roughness = true, displacement = nothing)

pbrt-v4's conductor: one GGX reflection lobe with the Fresnel of the complex IOR ior + i extinction (Blender's Metallic BSDF with its physical conductor Fresnel), single scattering, as pbrt renders it. Instead of its IOR a metal can be given its reflectance, its colour at normal incidence, as pbrt converts it (IOR 1 + i 2√r/√(1 - r) at each wavelength). Not both.

  • ior, extinction: a colour, a texture, or a spectrum (the measured metals Gold(), Silver(), Copper(), Aluminum() and Brass() are spectra).

  • roughness: one value, or (u, v) along the tangent and across it; with remap_roughness the GGX alpha is pbrt's of it.

For Blender's artist-friendly metal with an edge tint, use Metallic.

source
Hikari.ConductorFresnel Type

A conductor's Fresnel from its complex IOR, eta and k at each wavelength: pbrt-v4's FrComplex. Built at the path's wavelengths (measured spectra have no RGB).

Crossings are surface within radius of centre (in x and y) and above floor.

DDAMajorantIterator

3D DDA iterator for traversing voxels along a ray through a majorant grid. Returns per-voxel majorant bounds for tight delta tracking.

Following PBRT-v4's DDAMajorantIterator implementation. The iterator state is immutable - dda_next returns a new iterator with updated state.

Note: Uses NTuple instead of Vec types for GPU compatibility.

Create an empty/invalid DDA iterator (for rays that miss the grid)

A native file input decoded only when its consumer needs the field.

source
Hikari.DenoiseConfig Type
julia
DenoiseConfig

Configuration parameters for the à-trous wavelet denoiser.

Fields

  • iterations: Number of filter passes (each doubles the filter radius)

  • sigma_color: Color edge-stopping threshold (luminance sensitivity)

  • sigma_normal: Normal edge-stopping threshold (angular sensitivity)

  • sigma_depth: Depth edge-stopping threshold (distance sensitivity)

source
Hikari.DenoiseConfig Method
julia
DenoiseConfig(; iterations=4, sigma_color=1.0, sigma_normal=64.0,
                sigma_depth=0.1)

Create a denoiser configuration with sensible defaults.

Units (post log-luminance / relative-depth fix):

  • sigma_color is in stops (log2 luminance diff) — 1.0 means a 2× ratio weighted at exp(-1) ≈ 0.37. Lower = sharper edges.

  • sigma_normal is the exponent on clamp(dot(n_p, n_q), 0, 1). Higher = more sensitive to normal differences.

  • sigma_depth is relative depth tolerance (fraction of local depth) — 0.1 means a 10% depth diff per filter step weighted at exp(-1).

There is no use_variance: real SVGF needs temporal variance from sample history, which a Film does not store, and the spatial substitute was actively harmful — it mistakes texture for noise. See weight_color.

source
Hikari.DenoisePlan Type

What denoise! keeps between calls: the ping-pong partner of the framebuffer, and the compiled plan that filters into it.

Keyed on the film's framebuffer and the iteration count, because both are baked when the plan is compiled — the passes name the buffers, and how many there are is config.iterations. The sigmas are not: they ride Refs and are read at record time, so turning the filter up mid-session costs nothing.

source
Hikari.Denoiser Type
julia
Denoiser

How denoise! cleans a film's noise: DenoiseConfig, an à-trous filter on the GPU, or OIDN, Intel Open Image Denoise's network.

DeviceMemory(backend)

The device allocations one VolPathState owns.

Constructed from a KernelAbstractions backend because that is what a renderer has; it resolves the Mantle device once and allocates from that device's pool thereafter. One per state, and it dies with the state.

source
Hikari.DeviceMemory Method
julia
DeviceMemory()

Memory that belongs to no device: the owner of a host-side template (a Film before Film(backend, film) uploads it). It holds nothing, so free! returns at once and there is no finalizer.

source
Hikari.Dielectric Type

pbrt-v4's DielectricMaterial: one GGX glass lobe with the dielectric Fresnel, single scattering, in pbrt's convention. ior is a number, a texture, or a spectrum that disperses the path's wavelengths; the roughness along and across the tangent is remapped to the GGX alpha with remap_roughness, as pbrt does.

source
Hikari.DielectricFresnel Type

The real dielectric Fresnel at the lobe's IOR, tinting what it reflects and what it lets through.

source
Hikari.Diffuse Type
julia
Diffuse(; color = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8), roughness = 0, normal = nothing, displacement = nothing)

Blender's Diffuse BSDF: Lambert, or with roughness (0 to 1) the energy-preserving Oren-Nayar lobe Cycles and OpenPBR use. Any field takes a number, a colour, an image or a node graph.

  • color: the albedo; its alpha cuts the surface out.

  • normal: the shading normal, for a bump or normal_map node; nothing is the surface's own.

  • displacement: a height the shading normal is bumped by, as pbrt's displacement.

A Diffuse is a shader graph node, including when it is the only node. Its constants are folded into its BSDF program and need no values dispatch.

source
Hikari.DiffuseAreaLight Type
julia
DiffuseAreaLight{LeTex}

Per-triangle area light for emissive surfaces. Following pbrt-v4's DiffuseAreaLight, stores triangle geometry for sampling and emission texture/color for evaluation.

Each emissive triangle creates one DiffuseAreaLight. The light sampler (PowerLightSampler) includes these for importance sampling, enabling MIS with BSDF sampling.

Fields

  • vertices: Triangle vertex positions (for uniform sampling)

  • normal: Geometric normal of the triangle

  • area: Triangle area (precomputed)

  • uv: Vertex UV coordinates (for texture evaluation via barycentric interpolation)

  • Le: Emitted radiance — RGBSpectrum for constant, TextureRef for textured emission

  • scale: Intensity multiplier applied to Le

  • two_sided: If true, emits from both sides of the surface

source
Hikari.DiffuseBSDF Type

Blender's Diffuse BSDF: Lambert, or Cycles' energy-preserving Oren-Nayar with roughness.

source
Hikari.DiffuseLobe Type

Cycles' energy-preserving Oren-Nayar (OpenPBR's): a + b t for single scattering and ms for the light that scatters more than once, scaled by what single scattering leaves at the light's angle. Lambert is a = 1/π, b = 0, ms = 0.

source
Hikari.DiffuseLobe Method

Cycles' bsdf_oren_nayar_setup for color and roughness seen from wo, in the frame of n; Lambert where the roughness is almost zero.

source
Hikari.DiffuseTransmission Type
julia
DiffuseTransmission(; reflectance = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), transmittance = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), scale = 1,
                    displacement = nothing)

pbrt-v4's diffuse transmission: Lambert reflection of reflectance and Lambert transmission of transmittance, both times scale, for paper, thin fabric or leaves. Blender's equivalent is an Add of a Diffuse and a Translucent.

DirectionCone

Represents a cone of directions with axis w and half-angle cosθ.

  • cosθ = 1: point direction (degenerate cone)

  • cosθ = -1: entire sphere

Hikari.DirectionalLight Type

Directional light does not take medium interface, since only reasonable interface for it is vacuum, otherwise all the light would've been absorbed by the medium, since the light is infinitely far away.

source
Hikari.DirectionalLight Method
julia
DirectionalLight(rgb::RGB{Float32}, direction; illuminance=nothing)

Create a DirectionalLight from RGB color with automatic spectral conversion and photometric normalization, matching pbrt-v4's light creation pattern.

Arguments

  • rgb: RGB color (intensity encoded in color values)

  • direction: Direction the light travels (away from source)

  • illuminance: Optional target illuminance in lux. If specified, overrides the RGB intensity.

Example

julia
# Directional light traveling in -Y direction (sunlight from above)
light = DirectionalLight(RGB{Float32}(1f0, 1f0, 1f0), Vec3f(0, -1, 0))
source
Hikari.Distribution2D Type
julia
Distribution2D{V<:AbstractVector{Float32}, M<:AbstractMatrix{Float32}}

GPU-compatible 2D distribution that stores all data in flat arrays/matrices. Avoids nested device arrays which cause SPIR-V validation errors on OpenCL.

The conditional distribution data is stored as 2D matrices where each column represents one conditional distribution:

  • conditional_func[i, v] = func value at index i for row v

  • conditional_cdf[i, v] = cdf value at index i for row v

  • conditional_func_int[v] = func_int for row v

source
Hikari.Distribution2D Method
julia
Distribution2D(func::Matrix{Float32})

Construct a GPU-friendly 2D distribution directly from a function matrix. The matrix has dimensions (nv, nu) where nv is height (rows) and nu is width (columns).

source
Hikari.Emission Type
julia
Emission(; color = (1, 1, 1), strength = 1, two_sided = false)

Blender's Emission: a surface that emits radiance strength times color, which takes a colour or an image. A mesh of it is a light, each triangle an area light sampled for direct lighting, as pbrt's AreaLightSource "diffuse"; with two_sided it emits from its back as well. As a MediumInterface's emission it makes a lit surface of any material, and in a Mix or Add it is Blender's Emission shader, which the paths that hit it find.

Its radiance is normalized as pbrt-v4 normalizes an area light's: strength 1 of a white color is one nit.

source
Hikari.Emission Method
julia
Emission(area_light::PBRTEntity)

The emission of a pbrt AreaLightSource "diffuse" record.

Applies pbrt-v4's photometric normalization from lights.cpp DiffuseAreaLight::Create, which scales so radiance is equivalent to 1 nit:

julia
scale /= SpectrumToPhotometric(L)

Emission normalizes by D65's, so its strength is pbrt's scale times D65's over the ACTUAL emitter spectrum's. For an RGBIlluminantSpectrum the two coincide — pbrt and Hikari both special-case it back to the colour space's illuminant — but that is a property of that spectrum type, not a licence to hardcode D65.

Both importers (Hikari's pbrt_build_scene and RayMakie's pbrt_to_makie) go through here so they cannot drift apart.

source
Hikari.EmissionBSDF Type

Blender's Emission: radiance strength times color, found by the paths that hit it.

Environment map texture for HDR image-based lighting. Supports sampling by direction vector (for environment lights). Includes importance sampling distribution based on luminance.

Uses equal-area (octahedral) mapping like pbrt-v4's ImageInfiniteLight. Expects SQUARE images in equal-area format.

Hikari.EnvironmentMap Method

Everywhere()

Every crossing of the metaball field is surface.

source
Hikari.F82Tint Type

Cycles' F82 tint, Gulbrandsen's artist-friendly conductor: f0 at normal incidence, tint at about 82°, optionally under a thin film.

source
Hikari.FEMElements Type
julia
FEMElements(cx, cy, cf, warp, metadata, opaque)

The scene's FEM geometry, as the traversal sees it: three coefficient blocks (x, y, and the field), the out-of-plane scale the field is drawn at, per-cell metadata carrying the material, and whether that material stops shadow rays (see opaque).

This is the value that goes on VulkanTLAS.procedural. It reaches the kernel by Adapt, like every other device array on the accel.

source
Hikari.FEMFieldTexture Type
julia
FEMFieldTexture(coeffs, ramp; vmin, vmax)

The FEM solution as a texture: evaluates the element's own polynomial at the hit's reference coordinate and looks the value up in a colour ramp.

A TEXTURE and not a shading path. Writing a colour into the hit would bypass the BSDF, the lights, the shadows and the path continuation — an albedo viewer rather than a renderer. Bound to any material's parameter, the field composes with every BSDF Hikari has, and material dispatch stays MultiTypeSet untouched.

VertexColorTexture is the precedent and the shape is the same: read face_idx off the hit to pick the data, read the hit's surface coordinate to interpolate. What differs is only that a per-face colour is interpolated linearly and a field is evaluated — uv carries ξ, which the intersection put there.

source
Hikari.FEMFieldTexture Method

Build one from a coefficient block and any Makie-style colour ramp.

source
Hikari.FEMHit Type

The traversal's running best hit.

The loop carries this ITSELF rather than reading it back, because an inline ray query carries no hit attributes for a generated intersection — get_barycentrics is triangles only. The traversal commits only an IMPROVING t, which makes this local best the one it finally commits.

source
Hikari.FEMMaterial Type
julia
FEMMaterial(surface::Material, cx, cy, cf; warp, colormap, colorrange)
FEMMaterial(cx, cy, cf; warp, colormap, colorrange)

Curved finite elements: a material that carries its own geometry.

cx, cy, cf are FEM_NMONO x ncells coefficient blocks — the element's x and y maps and the solution — and warp is how far the solution displaces the element out of plane.

surface is any Hikari material, and the field is merged into whatever that material uses as its colour (merge_color_with_material). That is the entire argument for the field being a texture rather than a shading path: it composes, so a solution can be matte, lacquered, or polished metal without any of those knowing what an element is.

julia
FEMMaterial(cx, cy, cf)                          # matte
FEMMaterial(CoatedDiffuse(), cx, cy, cf)         # the field under a clear coat
FEMMaterial(Conductor(roughness = 0.08), cx, cy, cf)   # tinted metal

Defaults to Diffuse(), which is the material a colour with no material means everywhere else in the renderer.

source
Hikari.Film Method
julia
Film(backend, film::Film) -> Film

film's layers on backend, in memory this film owns.

Replaces Adapt.adapt(backend, film), which was doing the allocating — adapt converts, and a conversion that reaches for an allocator has nowhere to put one, which is why the result could only ever be freed by the GC. free!(film) releases these; forgetting it retires them instead of losing them.

filter_table stays on the host: it is read when the plans are built, never by a kernel. iteration_index is shared with film, as it was before — it is the progressive sample counter, and two films disagreeing about it is the bug.

  • filter: Pixel reconstruction filter (default: LanczosSinc)

  • crop_bounds: Region to render in [0,1] range (default: full image)

source
Hikari.GLTF Type
julia
GLTF(; base_color_factor = (1, 1, 1, 1), base_color_texture = nothing, metallic_factor = 1,
     roughness_factor = 1, metallic_roughness_texture = nothing, normal_texture = nothing, normal_scale = 1,
     emissive_factor = (0, 0, 0), emissive_texture = nothing, emissive_strength = 1, alpha_mode = :opaque,
     alpha_cutoff = 0.5, ior = 1.5, transmission_factor = 0, transmission_texture = nothing,
     clearcoat_factor = 0, clearcoat_texture = nothing, clearcoat_roughness_factor = 0,
     clearcoat_roughness_texture = nothing, clearcoat_normal_texture = nothing, sheen_color_factor = (0, 0, 0),
     sheen_color_texture = nothing, sheen_roughness_factor = 0, sheen_roughness_texture = nothing,
     specular_factor = 1, specular_texture = nothing, specular_color_factor = (1, 1, 1),
     specular_color_texture = nothing, iridescence_factor = 0, iridescence_ior = 1.3,
     iridescence_thickness = 400, anisotropy_strength = 0, anisotropy_rotation = 0)

A glTF 2.0 material, its metallic-roughness model and the KHR_materials_* extensions (ior, transmission, clearcoat, sheen, specular, emissive strength, iridescence, anisotropy), with glTF's names. Each factor multiplies its texture, an image sampled at the uv, as glTF defines them: metallic is the blue channel of metallic_roughness_texture and roughness its green; the colour textures are taken as linear, decoded from sRGB. alpha_mode is :opaque, :mask (cut out below alpha_cutoff) or :blend. It renders as the Principled BSDF Blender's glTF importer makes of it.

GPU-compatible filter parameters for kernel use. For filters requiring tabulated importance sampling (Gaussian, Mitchell, Lanczos), the table data must be passed separately to the kernel.

GPUFilterSamplerData

GPU-compatible tabulated data for importance sampling filters. Stores the distribution data needed for sampling Gaussian/Mitchell/Lanczos filters.

This matches pbrt-v4's FilterSampler which uses PiecewiseConstant2D.

Build GPU-compatible filter sampler data from a filter, or from the GPUFilterParams a film or integrator keeps of one. Returns nothing for Box/Triangle filters (they use analytical sampling).

GatheredRef{M}

A hit for the closure kernel of BSDF nodes M: its index in surface_hits and where its values kernel left its inputs.

GatheredShader{M}

The shader a closure kernel of BSDF nodes M shades a hit with: the inputs its values kernel gathered and its closure program.

The values a closure kernel reads for one hit, by the numbers closure_program gave them: what the values kernel stored (gather_inputs!).

source
Hikari.GaussianFilter Type
julia
GaussianFilter(radius=Point2f(1.5, 1.5), sigma=0.5)

Gaussian filter with configurable sigma. The filter is truncated at the radius and normalized by subtracting the value at the boundary.

source
Hikari.GeneratedGeometry Type
julia
abstract type GeneratedGeometry <: Material

A material that carries its own geometry.

A plot normally hands a renderer triangles. Some things are not triangles: a finite element is a polynomial patch, a subdivision surface is a limit, an implicit surface is a root. What those share is that the TRIANGLES ARE A CHOICE — how many, and how close — and the code that knows how to make them belongs to whoever owns the data.

Subtype this and implement tessellate. That is the whole interface: mesh!(scene, anything; material = yours) then draws it, rasterised and path traced, from the same triangles. The anything is what a backend that has never heard of your material falls back to.

julia
struct MyElements <: Hikari.GeneratedGeometry
    nodes::Matrix{Float64}
    tolerance::Float64
end

Hikari.tessellate(m::MyElements) = GeometryBasics.Mesh(positions, faces)

If you can solve a ray against your surface, add a push! method and the tracer stops approximating — one box per primitive goes into the acceleration structure and the hit is exact at any zoom, while the rasteriser goes on using tessellate. Dispatch picks it; nothing branches on a flag:

julia
Base.push!(scene::Hikari.Scene, ::Any, m::MyElements; transform) = ...

FEMMaterial in fem.jl is a worked example of both halves.

source
Hikari.Glossy Type
julia
Glossy(; color = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8), roughness = 0.5, anisotropy = 0, rotation = 0, normal = nothing,
       tangent = nothing, distribution = :multi_ggx)

Blender's Glossy BSDF with the multiscatter GGX distribution: a microfacet reflection tinted by color at every angle, a mirror at no roughness. distribution is the constant :multi_ggx (Blender's default), :ggx or :beckmann; the latter two use single scattering.

Blender's Glossy BSDF: GGX reflection of color, no Fresnel.

A participating medium with spatially varying density. Uses a 3D grid for density and a coarser majorant grid for efficient sampling.

Henyey-Greenstein phase function for anisotropic scattering.

Simple iterator that returns a single majorant segment for homogeneous media. Provides consistent iterator interface with DDAMajorantIterator.

A participating medium with constant properties throughout. Simplest medium type - majorant equals actual extinction everywhere. ior: the index of the surface it lies under, for light sampling through Snell's window (see refracting); 0 for a medium light reaches in straight lines.

KernelShapes(shapes, scales)

Every particle's kernel (see Anisotropic): the symmetric matrix M whose dᵀ M d takes the place of |d|²/R² in Wyvill's polynomial, and the kernel's scale.

Hikari.LanczosSincFilter Type
julia
LanczosSincFilter(radius=Point2f(4.0, 4.0), tau=3.0)

Lanczos-windowed sinc filter for high-quality reconstruction. The sinc function is windowed by another sinc to reduce ringing.

source
Hikari.LayeredBSDF Type

pbrt-v4's LayeredBxDF: the interface top over bottom (tuples of weighted lobes, pbrt's convention, in the local frame), thickness apart, with a medium of single-scattering albedo and Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry g between them (none for a black albedo); estimated by n_samples random walks of at most max_depth bounces. TwoSided mirrors it for light from below, as pbrt's coated materials are. In the shading frame of n and t. dispersive where the interface's IOR is a spectrum, taken at the path's first wavelength: the path's others end where it meets the BSDF, as pbrt's coated materials end them in GetBxDF (terminates_at_vertex).

source
Hikari.LayeredBSDF Method
julia
LayeredBSDF{TwoSided}(top, bottom, ns, dpdus, thickness, albedo, g, max_depth, n_samples, lambda; dispersive)

The layered BSDF of top over bottom in the shading frame of ns and dpdus.

source
Hikari.LevelSetElements Type

The level set as the traversal sees it: the grid, the leaf (first word) and index-space corner of each box, the medium interface every hit carries, which way the values run.

Hikari.LevelSetHit Type

The traversal's running best hit: its t and where it is, in object space.

source
Hikari.LevelSetSurface Type
julia
LevelSetSurface(interface, tree::NanoTree; iso = 0, rising = false, region = Everywhere(), tile = 1)

The surface where tree's values cross iso, drawn with interface (a MediumInterface, or any material). rising says the values rise into what the surface encloses (an indicator, a density); otherwise they fall into it (a signed distance, negative inside). Crossings are surface where region says (see counts). Textures lie over it from above once every tile metres. Where a leaf has no neighbour the grid is taken to go on as at its edge: the band a grid was made in ends without a surface there.

source
Hikari.LightBVHNode Type
julia
LightBVHNode

BVH node for the light sampler. Stores unquantized LightBounds fields plus tree connectivity. Interior nodes store child1 index; child0 is always at node_idx + 1 (left child immediately follows parent in array).

Simplification vs pbrt-v4: we skip CompactLightBounds quantization. Node is ~64 bytes instead of 32, but avoids OctahedralVector/bit-packing complexity. With 37k lights this is ~5MB — negligible on GPU.

source
Hikari.LightBounds Type

LightBounds

Stores spatial and directional bounds for a light or group of lights. Used by BVHLightSampler for importance-based light selection.

Following pbrt-v4's LightBounds (lights.h:104-125).

Result of sampling a light source with spectral radiance.

GPU-compatible light sampler data structure. Stores alias table as flat arrays that can be uploaded to GPU.

Hikari.LobeBSDF Type

The BSDF a material makes at a hit: its weighted lobes, of which one is sampled in proportion to its share of total, and what the hit emits.

source
Hikari.LobeSetup Type

What a shader's lobes are set up with: Cycles' lookup tables, and whether the path regularizes (regularizes), which roughens a near-specular lobe as pbrt-v4's BSDF::Regularize does.

A lobe is roughened before its albedo and energy compensation are taken from the tables (setup_fresnel). Roughened after, as it was, it kept the compensation of the smoother lobe, and a rough glass lost 3 % of the light at each pass through it: a white furnace showed 0.967.

source
Hikari.LookupValue Type

One value of the lookup tables: its own element type, so the table's texture slot is known at compile time.

source
Hikari.LoopTopology Type

A triangle mesh with each face's neighbour across each of its edges, as pbrt's SDFace: v[k, face] its vertices, f[k, face] the face across the edge from v[k] to the next vertex (0 on a boundary), start a face of each vertex.

source
Hikari.MajorantGrid Type
julia
MajorantGrid

Coarse grid storing maximum extinction coefficients for DDA traversal. Used to provide tight majorant bounds in heterogeneous media.

Note: Uses Vec{3, Int32} instead of Vec3i (Int64) for GPU compatibility.

source
Hikari.MaterialQueues Type
julia
MaterialQueues

The surface hits waiting for their material's shading kernel: per slot s of the scene's materials set, sizes[s] indices into the shared surface_hits store at items[(s - 1) * capacity + 1 : s * capacity], and emits[s], whether the slot's type can emit (emits), which decides whether a hit at the depth limit is shaded at all.

The kernels that fill it (the trace, the medium sampling) take it as it is, whatever the materials. It was a tuple of queues typed per material type, so a new type changed the trace kernel's type and compiled it again, the biggest kernel there is, with every node edit.

source
Hikari.MaterialQueues Method
julia
MaterialQueues(materials::StaticMultiTypeSet, capacity, mem)

A segment of capacity hits for every slot of materials, in memory mem owns.

source
Hikari.MatrixCamera Type
julia
MatrixCamera <: Camera

A camera defined by view and projection matrices, matching the convention used by Makie's Camera struct (OpenGL-style: camera looks along -z in camera space).

This is a fallback camera for scenes that don't use Camera3D (e.g. Axis3 which uses its own camera type but still sets view/projection matrices on the scene camera).

The view matrix is world-to-camera, and the projection matrix is camera-to-clip (NDC). Both use OpenGL conventions (right-handed, camera looks along -z, clip z in [-1, 1]).

source
Hikari.MatrixCamera Method

MatrixCamera(view, projection, resolution, screen_window)

source
Hikari.MediumInteraction Type
julia
MediumInteraction

Represents an interaction point within a participating medium. Created when a real scattering event occurs during delta tracking.

source
Hikari.MediumInterface Type
julia
MediumInterface{M<:Material, I, O}

Material wrapper that combines a surface BSDF with medium boundaries. Surfaces define boundaries between media.

Emission is handled separately by DiffuseAreaLight (registered per-triangle in scene.lights, not on the material).

Fields

  • material: The underlying BSDF material (e.g., Diffuse, Glass)

  • inside: Medium for inside the surface, or nothing for vacuum

  • outside: Medium for outside the surface, or nothing for vacuum

  • shadows: 0 (the default) and the surface blocks shadow rays, as a surface with a BSDF does in pbrt-v4. An index of refraction and shadow rays pass through it, weighted by the Fresnel transmittance of a dielectric of that index, and cross into the medium on the other side, unbent. A water surface needs this: the sun is a delta light only shadow rays reach, and with the surface opaque to them no sunlight ever lit the water inside, which then glowed only from the few paths that happened to refract out to the sky (dark, and very noisy). What is lost is the refraction of the light on its way in, the caustics, as in most production renderers.

Usage

julia
# Glass with fog inside
MediumInterface(Glass(); inside=fog)

# Simple material with no medium transition
MediumInterface(Diffuse(color = (0.8, 0.2, 0.2)))
source

source
Hikari.MetaballSurface Type
julia
MetaballSurface(interface, points, radius; iso, step = radius / 6, lattice = 4, region = Everywhere(), tile = 1)
MetaballSurface(interface, mb::Metaballs; lattice = 4, region = Everywhere(), tile = 1)

A metaball surface as a material that carries its geometry (see Metaballs): the surface at level iso of points' field, drawn with interface (a MediumInterface, or any material), where region says crossings are surface (see counts). Its textures (a bump, say) are laid over it from above, once every tile metres in x and y. Given metaballs already built (for other uses of the same field), it draws them as they are.

Rays find it in the field sampled lattice times across each cell that can hold the surface and interpolated trilinearly, one look-up for the hundreds of particles the field sums; the normal is the exact field's.

source
Hikari.Metaballs Type
julia
Metaballs(points, radius; iso, step = radius / 6, anisotropy = nothing, chunk = 32768, backend)

The surface at level iso of the metaball field of points, each contributing (1 - d²/radius²)³ within radius. step is the spacing of the field samples a ray takes where the surface may be; features thinner than it can be missed. The particles are sorted into cells on the host and the cells classified on backend, chunk cells a launch. With anisotropy = Anisotropic() every particle's kernel is an ellipsoid shaped by its neighbours instead of a ball (see Anisotropic).

source
Hikari.Metallic Type
julia
Metallic(; base_color = (0.617, 0.577, 0.540), edge_tint = (0.695, 0.726, 0.770), roughness = 0.5,
         anisotropy = 0, rotation = 0, normal = nothing, tangent = nothing,
         thin_film_thickness = 0, thin_film_ior = 1.33, distribution = :multi_ggx,
         fresnel_type = :f82, ior = (2.757, 2.513, 2.231), extinction = (3.867, 3.404, 3.009))

Blender's Metallic BSDF with the F82 tint Fresnel: base_color at normal incidence, edge_tint towards grazing angles. Set fresnel_type = :physical_conductor to use the complex index ior + i extinction instead. All inputs except fresnel_type and distribution can be images or node graphs. For measured spectra and pbrt's roughness convention, use Conductor. distribution is the constant :multi_ggx (Blender's default), :ggx or :beckmann; the latter two use single scattering.

source
Hikari.MetallicBSDF Type

Blender's Metallic BSDF: GGX reflection with the F82 tint of a conductor.

source
Hikari.MicrofacetConvention Type

Where Cycles' microfacets and pbrt-v4's differ, which convention a lobe follows: below which roughness it is a mirror, and whether refraction scales the radiance it carries by 1/η². Cycles' GGX and Beckmann are singular at αx·αy ≤ 2e-10 and do not scale. pbrt's is singular below max(αx, αy) = 1e-3 (EffectivelySmooth) and scales the radiance a path carries (PbrtRadiance) but not importance (PbrtImportance), which pbrt's layered BSDF transports on its way back.

source
Hikari.MicrofacetLobe Type

A microfacet lobe, as Cycles' bsdf_microfacet: reflection only (Mode :reflection), refraction only (:refraction), reflection and refraction (:glass), or the transmission of a thin glass, a reflection mirrored to the far side (:thin). energy scales single scattering up by what it misses, Cycles' multiscatter GGX, and is one for pbrt's single-scattering one; inv_abbe disperses the IOR over the wavelengths. C is the MicrofacetConvention it follows.

source
Hikari.MitchellFilter Type
julia
MitchellFilter(radius=Point2f(2.0, 2.0), B=1/3, C=1/3)

Mitchell-Netravali filter - a family of cubic filters parameterized by B and C. Default B=C=1/3 gives a good balance between ringing and blurring.

source
Hikari.Mix Type
julia
Mix(a, b; factor = 0.5)

Blender's Mix Shader: a where factor is 0, b where it is 1, which takes a number, an image or a node graph. Cycles and pbrt models combine in one shader graph. Ordinary scattering lobes are weighted together. A graph containing a layered pbrt model selects its complete BSDF at the vertex so its random-walk sampling PDF remains valid.

source
Hikari.NanoBlend Type
julia
NanoBlend(a::NanoTree, b::NanoTree, weight)

Two independently positioned NanoVDB fields, interpolated at the sampled world position. Missing voxels use each grid's own background. This descriptor retains the two input buffers and never constructs a third voxel array. weight must be finite and in [0,1]. A file-input consumer can pass its a, b and weight directly here without introducing a dependency on an editor package.

source
Hikari.NanoGridMedium Type
julia
NanoGridMedium(density; temperature=nothing, σ_a=RGBSpectrum(0),
               σ_s=RGBSpectrum(1), g=0, emission_scale=1,
               temperature_offset=0, temperature_scale=1, majorant_res=(64,64,64))

Smoke, clouds, or hot absorbing matter on device-built NanoVDB fields. density may be a NanoTree or a lazy NanoBlend. It multiplies the absorption and scattering coefficients (per metre); temperature is an optional independently positioned NanoTree in kelvin. Its thermal source radiance is Planck's law in W/(m² sr nm), multiplied by emission_scale. The integrator multiplies this source by local absorption, as required by Kirchhoff's law. Density zero therefore emits nothing. This is a thermal continuum model, not a combustion solver or a model of spectral line emission.

Temperature is interpreted as (value - temperature_offset) * temperature_scale. Unlike pbrt's peak-normalized blackbody, the physical source gets brighter with temperature. A separate grid is optional for non-emissive storm clouds.

source
Hikari.NanoRegion Type
julia
NanoRegion(field, centre, inner, outer)

field (a NanoTree or NanoBlend) only round a vertical axis through centre (x, y): in full out to inner, eased to nothing at outer (smoothstep in the distance from the axis), nothing beyond. For a field recorded over a box but drawn only where a round region of the scene is, such as a whirlpool's whitewater beside the water traced inside a cylinder. Majorants of field bound it.

source
Hikari.NanoTree Type
julia
NanoTree

A NanoVDB float grid in a device buffer of 32-bit words (words, adapted to the device with the tree): where its nodes start (in words, from 0), how many there are, and its voxels' placement in the world, voxel metres apart, the centre of voxel (0, 0, 0) half a voxel inside lo. Values outside every leaf and tile are background.

source
Hikari.NanoTree Method
julia
NanoTree(origins, values, lo, voxel; background = 0, backend)

The NanoVDB float grid of the leaves at origins (device, Vec{3,Int32} index-space corners, multiples of 8, distinct) with values (device, 512 per leaf in NanoVDB's order, x slowest: see leaf_coord_to_offset), voxels voxel apart from lo (see NanoTree). The root has a tile per upper node the leaves reach; the nodes follow it in NanoVDB's order: uppers, lowers, leaves.

source
Hikari.NanoVDBMedium Type
julia
NanoVDBMedium

Direct NanoVDB volume sampling medium that keeps the buffer in native format. Matches pbrt-v4's NanoVDBMedium implementation exactly.

The buffer contains the entire decompressed NanoVDB grid data. Tree traversal is done on-the-fly using byte offsets.

source
Hikari.NanoVDBMedium Method
julia
NanoVDBMedium(data::Array{Float32,3}; bounds, σ_a, σ_s, g, majorant_res, buffer_alloc)

Construct a NanoVDBMedium from a dense 3D array by building a sparse NanoVDB tree. Only leaf blocks (8³) containing non-zero voxels are stored, giving significant memory savings for sparse volumetric data like cloud fields.

Arguments

  • data: Dense 3D Float32 array of density/opacity values

  • bounds: World-space bounding box (Bounds3)

  • σ_a: Absorption coefficient (default: 0 for pure scattering clouds)

  • σ_s: Scattering coefficient (default: 1)

  • g: Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry parameter

  • majorant_res: Resolution of majorant grid (default: 64³)

  • buffer_alloc: Array constructor for target device (default: Vector{UInt8})

source
Hikari.NanoVDBMedium Method
julia
NanoVDBMedium(filepath::String; σ_a, σ_s, g, transform, majorant_res)

Construct a NanoVDBMedium from a NanoVDB file.

Arguments

  • filepath: Path to the .nvdb file

  • σ_a: Absorption coefficient (RGBSpectrum)

  • σ_s: Scattering coefficient (RGBSpectrum)

  • g: Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry parameter

  • transform: Optional 3x3 rotation matrix (medium-to-world, like pbrt's Rotate)

  • majorant_res: Resolution of majorant grid (default 64³)

For pbrt bunny-cloud scene, use: transform = RotZ(π) * RotX(π/2) # Rotate 180° around Z, then 90° around X

source
Hikari.NoFresnel Type

No Fresnel: the lobe reflects and refracts all, its colour in its weight. color is what its energy compensation darkens towards.

source
Hikari.NodeCore Type

One node of a texture graph, as the interpreter runs it: an operation, its settings, its inputs (TexNode outputs of other nodes, or Float32 constants) and the width of each output (1 for a scalar, 3 for a vector).

source
Hikari.NodeInstr Type

One instruction of a compiled node program. arg[i] is the stack offset input i is read from (NO_SLOT: the constant k[i]), and bit i of wide says whether that offset holds a vector. out[j] is where output j is stored (NO_SLOT: not needed), bit j of outwide whether it is a vector. mode holds the node's settings, such as a math operation or a noise type. F is the program's NodeFeature bits. In a closure program, the first instruction uses the upper three outwide bits for its conservative storage bound (zero: general).

source
Hikari.NullMaterial Type
julia
NullMaterial

Marker material for medium-boundary surfaces that have no BSDF. Pbrt-v4 sets the surface material to nullptr; rays cross the boundary transparently and only the medium swap fires. In Hikari we make push!(scene.materials, ::NullMaterial) return an invalid SetKey(), so the existing !is_valid(mi.material) checks in the primary- and shadow-ray paths identify the surface as a null interface and skip BSDF sampling.

A null surface with emission is a see-through emitter: its emission is added where a ray crosses it, then the ray (and every shadow ray) passes on. pbrt-v4 ignores area lights on interface materials; this is what a glowing sheet floating in a scene needs.

Usage:

julia
push!(scene, bounding_mesh, MediumInterface(NullMaterial(); inside=medium))
glow = MediumInterface(NullMaterial(); emission=Emission(color=Texture(img), two_sided=true))
source

julia
OIDN(; quality = :high, guides = true)

Denoise with Intel Open Image Denoise's ray tracing filter, on the CPU. quality is :fast, :balanced or :high. With guides the filter also gets the film's albedo and normal (see fill_aux_buffers!), noise-free, which keep the edges and textures of what the camera sees first.

source
Hikari.OpenPBR Type
julia
OpenPBR(; base_weight = 1, base_color = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8), base_metalness = 0, base_diffuse_roughness = 0,
        specular_weight = 1, specular_color = (1, 1, 1), specular_roughness = 0.3,
        specular_roughness_anisotropy = 0, specular_ior = 1.5, transmission_weight = 0,
        transmission_color = (1, 1, 1), transmission_dispersion_scale = 0,
        transmission_dispersion_abbe_number = 20, subsurface_weight = 0, subsurface_color = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8),
        subsurface_radius = 1, subsurface_radius_scale = (1, 0.5, 0.25), subsurface_scatter_anisotropy = 0,
        fuzz_weight = 0, fuzz_color = (1, 1, 1), fuzz_roughness = 0.5, coat_weight = 0, coat_color = (1, 1, 1),
        coat_roughness = 0, coat_ior = 1.6, thin_film_weight = 0, thin_film_thickness = 0.5,
        thin_film_ior = 1.4, emission_luminance = 0, emission_color = (1, 1, 1), geometry_opacity = 1,
        geometry_thin_walled = false, geometry_normal = nothing, geometry_coat_normal = nothing,
        geometry_tangent = nothing)

An OpenPBR Surface, with OpenPBR's names and defaults, rendered as the Principled BSDF it corresponds to in Blender. What Principled has no input for is approximated: the transmission and subsurface colours tint the base where their weight is the constant one, fuzz is sheen, and coat darkening, coat anisotropy and the transmission depth and scattering are not modelled. thin_film_thickness is in micrometres, emission_luminance in nits.

Hikari.PCG32State Type

PCG32State

GPU-compatible immutable PCG32 random number generator state. Uses tuple-like struct for stack allocation on GPU.

source
Hikari.PerRun Type
julia
PerRun{C <: Camera}

The values a recorded sample reads per run — the camera, the initial medium, the filter parameters, the sample index — as the GPURefs the plan's commands hold the address of, and what each was last stored with. A call argument cannot announce itself, so identity against stored_* is how a sample knows what to store, and a still scene stores nothing.

Parametric in the camera type, and reached through VolPath.perrun, a field typed as the small union over the camera types — NOT through VolPathState.plans: that field is Any, and a compare or a store made through it was a dynamic call that boxed the camera it was handed, 684 bytes every sample of a still scene. Through the union the compare is bitwise and the store is a typed ref[] = x.

source
Hikari.PointLight Method
julia
PointLight(rgb::RGB{Float32}, position; power=nothing)
PointLight(rgb::RGB, position; power=nothing)

Create a PointLight from RGB color with automatic spectral conversion and photometric normalization, matching pbrt-v4's light creation pattern.

Converts RGB to RGBIlluminantSpectrum and applies photometric normalization: scale = 1 / SpectrumToPhotometric(spectrum) where SpectrumToPhotometric extracts the D65 illuminant component.

Arguments

  • rgb: RGB color (intensity encoded in color values, e.g., RGB(50,50,50) for bright white)

  • position: World-space position of the light

  • power: Optional radiant power in Watts. If specified, overrides the RGB intensity.

Example

julia
# Equivalent to pbrt-v4's: LightSource "point" "rgb I" [50 50 50]
light = PointLight(RGB{Float32}(50f0, 50f0, 50f0), Vec3f(10, 10, 10))

# Or with Makie's RGBf:
light = PointLight(RGBf(50, 50, 50), Vec3f(10, 10, 10))
source
Hikari.PowerLightSampler Type
julia
PowerLightSampler

Sample lights proportional to their total power using an alias table. O(1) sampling with O(N) construction. Good for scenes with varying light intensities.

Following pbrt-v4's PowerLightSampler which uses light.Phi() to estimate power.

source
Hikari.Principled Type
julia
Principled(; base_color = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8), metallic = 0, roughness = 0.5, ior = 1.5, alpha = 1,
           normal = nothing, diffuse_roughness = 0, subsurface_weight = 0, subsurface_radius = (1, 0.2, 0.1),
           subsurface_scale = 0.05, subsurface_ior = 1.4, subsurface_anisotropy = 0, specular_ior_level = 0.5,
           specular_tint = (1, 1, 1), anisotropic = 0, anisotropic_rotation = 0, tangent = nothing,
           transmission_weight = 0, transmission_dispersion_scale = 0, transmission_dispersion_abbe_number = 20,
           coat_weight = 0, coat_roughness = 0.03, coat_ior = 1.5, coat_tint = (1, 1, 1), coat_normal = nothing,
           sheen_weight = 0, sheen_roughness = 0.5, sheen_tint = (1, 1, 1), emission_color = (1, 1, 1),
           emission_strength = 0, thin_film_thickness = 0, thin_film_ior = 1.33, thin_wall = false,
           distribution = :multi_ggx)

Blender's Principled BSDF with every input it has, laid out as Cycles does: transparency, sheen and coat over the metal, transmission and the specular layer over the diffuse base. Each input except thin_wall and distribution takes a number, a colour, an image or a node graph. distribution is the constant :multi_ggx (Blender's default), :ggx or :beckmann for single scattering. Beckmann extends Blender's Principled node so all Glass configurations use this same path.

normal = nothing is the surface's shading normal and coat_normal = nothing is normal; the default tangent is Blender's, radial around the Z axis (here the world's, Blender's is the object's). With thin_wall, a constant, transmission and subsurface are those of a surface of no thickness. Emission is found by the paths that hit it; for a light, use Emission.

source

Principled(m::GLTF)

The Principled BSDF of a glTF material, as Blender's glTF importer makes it.

source
Hikari.Principled Method
julia
Principled(m::OpenPBR)

The Principled BSDF of an OpenPBR Surface, as Blender maps one onto the other.

source
Hikari.PrincipledBSDF Type

Blender's Principled BSDF, as Cycles' svm_node_closure_bsdf lays it out: transparency first, then sheen, coat and emission, which take from what is under them what they reflect, then the metal, transmission and the specular layer over subsurface and diffuse. ThinWall is its thin wall input, a constant; Subsurface and Emissive whether its subsurface weight and emission strength are not the constant zero, so a shader without them carries no code for them.

source
Hikari.PrincipledInputs Type

The inputs of a Principled BSDF, read off its instructions before its lobes are set up.

source
Hikari.RGBAlbedoSpectrum Type
julia
RGBAlbedoSpectrum

Bounded [0,1] spectrum for surface reflectance/albedo.

source
Hikari.RGBGridMedium Type
julia
RGBGridMedium

A participating medium with spatially varying per-voxel RGB absorption and scattering coefficients. Following pbrt-v4's RGBGridMedium implementation exactly.

Key design (matching pbrt-v4):

  • Optional σ_a grid: 3D array of RGBSpectrum absorption coefficients (if absent, defaults to 1.0)

  • Optional σ_s grid: 3D array of RGBSpectrum scattering coefficients (if absent, defaults to 1.0)

  • Optional Le grid: 3D array of RGBSpectrum emission coefficients (for emissive volumes)

  • sigma_scale: Global multiplier for σ_a and σ_s grids

  • Le_scale: Global multiplier for Le grid

  • The majorant grid stores sigma_scale * max(σ_a + σ_s) per coarse voxel

  • In SampleRay, uses unit σ_t since scaling is already in the majorant grid

source
Hikari.RGBGridMedium Method
julia
RGBGridMedium(; σ_a_grid, σ_s_grid, Le_grid, sigma_scale, Le_scale, g, bounds, transform, majorant_res)

Create an RGBGridMedium following pbrt-v4's design exactly.

At least one of σ_a_grid or σ_s_grid must be provided. The grids contain per-voxel RGBSpectrum values that are multiplied by sigma_scale (or Le_scale for emission).

Arguments

  • σ_a_grid: Optional 3D array of RGBSpectrum absorption coefficients

  • σ_s_grid: Optional 3D array of RGBSpectrum scattering coefficients

  • Le_grid: Optional 3D array of RGBSpectrum emission coefficients (requires σ_a_grid)

  • sigma_scale: Global multiplier for σ_a and σ_s grids (default: 1.0)

  • Le_scale: Global multiplier for Le grid (default: 0.0)

  • g: Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry parameter (default: 0.0)

  • bounds: Volume bounds in medium space (default: unit cube)

  • transform: Transform from medium to render space (default: identity)

  • majorant_res: Resolution of the majorant grid (default: 16³)

source
Hikari.RGBIlluminantSpectrum Type
julia
RGBIlluminantSpectrum

Illuminant spectrum for light sources, matching pbrt-v4's RGBIlluminantSpectrum. Stores RGB coefficients and multiplies by D65 illuminant when sampled.

Fields:

  • poly::RGBSigmoidPolynomial - Sigmoid polynomial for spectral shape

  • scale::Float32 - Scale factor (2 * max(r,g,b) from construction)

When sampled at wavelength λ: returns scale * poly(λ) * D65(λ)

source
Hikari.RGBSigmoidPolynomial Type
julia
RGBSigmoidPolynomial

Represents a smooth spectrum using a sigmoid-wrapped polynomial. The spectrum value at wavelength λ is: sigmoid(c0_λ² + c1_λ + c2) where sigmoid(x) = 0.5 + x / (2*sqrt(1 + x²))

This provides a smooth, bounded [0,1] spectrum from just 3 coefficients.

source
Hikari.RGBSigmoidPolynomial Method

Evaluate spectrum at wavelength λ (in nm)

source
Hikari.RGBToSpectrumTable Type
julia
RGBToSpectrumTable{V1, V5}

Precomputed lookup table for converting RGB colors to RGBSigmoidPolynomial coefficients. Uses trilinear interpolation for smooth results.

Parameterized by array types for GPU compatibility:

  • V1: 1D array type for scale (AbstractVector{Float32})

  • V5: 5D array type for coeffs (AbstractArray{Float32, 5})

Use to_gpu(ArrayType, table) to convert to GPU-compatible arrays.

Unbounded spectrum for illumination/emission. Scales the sigmoid polynomial to match the maximum RGB component.

Hikari.ShaderClosures Type

source
Hikari.ShaderContext Type

What a shader program reads besides the texture inputs: where the hit is seen from, the position's screen-space differentials (for bump), the shading tangent and the geometric normal, both facing outwards, the handedness of the tangent frame the uv map makes (1 where the bitangent ns × dpdus runs along increasing v, -1 where the uv map is mirrored), and where the hit is in the camera's space and on the image, for texture coordinates.

source
Hikari.ShaderGraph Type

A shader graph as a material holds it until it is compiled at push.

source
Hikari.ShaderInputs Type
julia
ShaderInputs(capacity, layout, mem)

What the values kernel of a shader (vp_shader_values_kernel!) hands its closure kernel for each surface hit, by the hit's index in surface_hits: the width floats its BSDF nodes read of the computed values (gather_inputs!), float g of hit h at (g - 1) * capacity + h, so the threads of a kernel read one float of consecutive hits together. program maps each material key to its BSDF program: a header offset per material type, followed by its instances' program indices. This lookup is independent of a hit's values pass, so a shader reading no computed inputs needs no values dispatch.

source
Hikari.ShaderMaterial Type
julia
ShaderMaterial(shader)

What Hikari renders Blender's BSDFs with (surface_material): a shader graph, as Blender's Material Output takes one, of BSDF nodes combined by mixes and sums, with node textures and bump at any of their inputs. The graph's values are compiled to one program, and its BSDF nodes are the material's type (bsdf_nodes). Cycles BSDF kernels use bounded local storage (bsdf_kernel_nodes), shared across node combinations and orderings. pbrt component and layered estimators use their graph adapters. A shader with transparency holds a second program, of its transparency alone (transparency_graph), which is all an alpha test runs.

On the device it also names its BSDF program (closure_program): its BSDF nodes read inputs floats gathered by the values kernel. Constant graphs skip that pass. A single pbrt node with elementary arithmetic or texture reads runs both programs in one small kernel; more involved graphs retain separate values and BSDF kernels so changes to their value-node families leave the BSDF kernel unchanged.

source
Hikari.ShaderNode Type

A shader in a graph: a BSDF node, or a Mix Shader or Add Shader of others. Build them with the functions in Hikari.TextureNodes and pass the result to ShaderMaterial.

source
Hikari.ShaderProgram Type

A shader's program on the device: its index among the stored programs of its type, and in its type the features it runs, so a kernel finds the program without branching over every type stored.

source
Hikari.SobolRNG Type
julia
SobolRNG{M}

GPU-compatible Sobol random number generator. Holds the Sobol matrices and precomputed parameters for ZSobol sampling.

This struct can be passed directly to GPU kernels via Adapt.jl integration. All sampling state is computed on-the-fly from pixel coordinates and sample index, making it stateless and thread-safe.

The matrices array contains both the Sobol generator matrices (indices 1:N) and the packed permutation table for ZSobol digit permutations (indices N+1:N+24). This avoids runtime tuple indexing which is broken on some GPU backends (e.g. Metal).

Fields

  • matrices::M: GPU array of Sobol generator matrices + packed permutations (UInt32)

  • log2_spp::Int32: log2 of samples per pixel

  • n_base4_digits::Int32: number of base-4 digits for Morton encoding

  • seed::UInt32: scrambling seed

  • width::Int32: image width (for pixel coordinate recovery)

  • pixels::Int32: number of pixels

  • lanes::Int32: samples of every pixel one wave of paths holds (see path_pixel_sample)

source

Hikari.SpotLight Method
julia
SpotLight(rgb::RGB{Float32}, position, target, total_width, falloff_start; power=nothing)

Create a SpotLight from RGB color with automatic spectral conversion and photometric normalization, matching pbrt-v4's light creation pattern.

Arguments

  • rgb: RGB color (intensity encoded in color values)

  • position::Point3f: World-space position of the spotlight

  • target::Point3f: Point the spotlight is aimed at

  • total_width::Float32: Total cone angle in degrees

  • falloff_start::Float32: Angle where intensity falloff begins (degrees)

  • power: Optional radiant power in Watts. If specified, overrides the RGB intensity.

Example

julia
# Spotlight with RGB color
light = SpotLight(RGB{Float32}(100f0, 100f0, 100f0), Point3f(0, 5, 0), Point3f(0, 0, 0), 30f0, 25f0)

Convenience constructor for SpotLight that takes position and target points.

Arguments

  • target::Point3f: Point the spotlight is aimed at

  • i::Spectrum: Light intensity/color

  • total_width::Float32: Total cone angle in degrees

  • falloff_start::Float32: Angle where intensity falloff begins (degrees)

  • scale::Float32: Photometric scale factor (default 1.0)

Example

julia
# Spotlight at (0, 5, 0) pointing at origin with 30° cone
light = SpotLight(Point3f(0, 5, 0), Point3f(0, 0, 0), RGBSpectrum(100f0), 30f0, 25f0)

source
Hikari.TextureFilterContext Type
julia
TextureFilterContext

Context for texture filtering, containing UV coordinates and screen-space derivatives. Following pbrt-v4's TextureEvalContext pattern.

Materials receive this context and pass it to eval_tex for proper texture filtering. The UV derivatives (dudx, dudy, dvdx, dvdy) are computed from:

  1. Surface partial derivatives (dpdu, dpdv) at intersection

  2. Screen-space position derivatives (dpdx, dpdy) from camera

These enable mipmap level selection and anisotropic filtering.

Hikari.VPMaterialEvalWorkItem Type
julia
VPMaterialEvalWorkItem

Surface interaction work item for VolPath. Similar to PWMaterialEvalWorkItem but includes medium transition info.

Following pbrt-v4's MaterialEvalWorkItem, stores surface partial derivatives for texture filtering. Screen-space derivatives (dudx, dudy, dvdx, dvdy) are computed on-the-fly during material evaluation using camera.Approximate_dp_dxy().

source
Hikari.VPMediumSampleWorkItem Type
julia
VPMediumSampleWorkItem

Work item for rays in medium that need delta tracking. Follows pbrt-v4's approach: intersection is found FIRST, then delta tracking runs with the known t_max distance.

If the ray reaches t_max without scattering/absorption, its surface hit goes to the material's shading kernel as any other does: hit is the record the trace found, which that kernel expands. A miss record when the ray escapes.

source
Hikari.VPMediumScatterWorkItem Type
julia
VPMediumScatterWorkItem

Work item for a real scattering event in a participating medium. Created when delta tracking samples a real scatter (not null scatter).

source
Hikari.VPRayWorkItem Type

VPRayWorkItem

Ray work item for volumetric path tracing. Includes medium index to track which medium the ray is currently in.

source
Hikari.VPShadowRayWorkItem Type
julia
VPShadowRayWorkItem

Shadow ray for direct lighting (works for both surface and volume scattering).

source
Hikari.VPSurfaceHit Type
julia
VPSurfaceHit

A ray's surface hit as the trace leaves it for the material's shading kernel: the hit record and where the ray's path state is. path > 0 is its index in the round's ray queue; path < 0 is -index into the arrivals, the paths a medium delivered to their surface with its transmittance applied. The shading kernel expands the record, so the surface is computed once, where it is shaded. primary tags a camera path whose constant scattering state is reconstructed instead of stored. Medium arrivals and subsequent rays always retain full state.

source
Hikari.VolPath Type
julia
VolPath <: Integrator

Volumetric path tracer using hero wavelength sampling and wavefront architecture.

Extends path tracing with support for participating media (fog, smoke, clouds). Uses delta tracking with null scattering for efficient medium traversal.

The main loop follows pbrt-v4's structure:

  1. If ray is in medium: run delta tracking

    • Absorption → terminate

    • Real scatter → sample direct light + phase function → continue

    • Null scatter → continue tracking

    • Escape medium → proceed to intersection

  2. Intersect with scene

  3. Handle surface (emission + BSDF) or environment light

source
Hikari.VolPath Method
julia
(vp::VolPath)(scene, film, camera)

Render using volumetric spectral wavefront path tracing.

Media are automatically extracted from MediumInterface materials during scene construction and stored in scene.media.

The render loop follows pbrt-v4's VolPathIntegrator:

  1. Generate camera rays (possibly in a medium)

  2. For each bounce: a. Delta tracking for rays in media → scatter or pass through b. Trace rays to find intersections c. Handle escaped rays (environment light) d. Handle surface hits (emission + direct lighting + BSDF sampling)

  3. Accumulate spectral samples to RGB

source
Hikari.VolPath Method
julia
VolPath(; max_depth=8, samples=64, russian_roulette_depth=3, regularize=true,
        max_component_value=10, filter=GaussianFilter(),
        accumulation_eltype=Float32, hw_accel=nothing)

Create a VolPath integrator for volumetric path tracing.

Arguments

  • max_depth: Maximum path depth

  • samples: Number of samples per pixel

  • russian_roulette_depth: Depth at which to start Russian roulette

  • regularize: Apply BSDF regularization to reduce fireflies (default: true). When enabled, near-specular BSDFs are roughened after the first non-specular bounce, following pbrt-v4's approach.

  • max_component_value: Maximum RGB component value before clamping (default: 10). When set to a finite value, RGB values are scaled down if any component exceeds this. This is pbrt-v4's firefly suppression mechanism. Try values like 10.0 or 100.0.

  • filter: Pixel reconstruction filter (default: GaussianFilter with radius 1.5, sigma 0.5). Supports BoxFilter, TriangleFilter, GaussianFilter, MitchellFilter, LanczosSincFilter. All filters use importance sampling with weight≈1 (pbrt-v4 compatible).

  • accumulation_eltype: Element type for RGB/weight accumulators (default: Float32). Use Float64 on backends that support double precision for higher accumulation precision.

  • hw_accel: Enable hardware ray tracing (default: false). When true and using LavaBackend, RayMakie creates an HWTLAS for hardware BVH traversal instead of software BVH. Dispatch happens on the accel type, not this flag.

Sensor simulation (ISO, exposure_time, white_balance) is applied during rendering via the PixelSensor on the integrator state, matching pbrt-v4. The framebuffer contains sensor-calibrated linear sRGB. Postprocessing is purely display mapping (exposure, tonemapping, gamma).
